name: Tungsten disulfide, monolayer
equilibrium_context: Direct two-dimensional semiconductor, A exciton at 2.00 eV at room temperature; K and K' valleys degenerate by time reversal
summary: Purely optical access - therefore free of any Volkov ambiguity and thus the most important independent check point of the entire Floquet debate.

driven_states.emergent_property: Light-dressed valley-selective shift of the exciton and band levels. Optical Stark effect: shift upward by up to 18 meV in only one valley, selected via the helicity. Bloch-Siegert shift: at lower photon energy the antiresonant contribution separates completely, 10.4 meV in one valley versus 18.6 meV in the other - the largest Bloch-Siegert shift ever measured directly in a solid.
driven_states.source: Sie et al., Nature Materials 14, 290 (2015), doi:10.1038/nmat4156
driven_states.caveat: The inverse problem compared with the photoemission cases: what is measured is not a band structure in momentum space but an exciton line. The assignment to Floquet-Bloch bands is an interpretation within a two-level picture. Excitonic many-body effects are not fully separated out. The classification as reproduced rests on independent work on the valley-selective Stark effect; the Bloch-Siegert shift itself remains single_group. The Volkov question does not apply, since no electrons are emitted.

threshold.quantity: none - Floquet dressing has no threshold

further_sources: Nat. Commun. 12 (2021), doi:10.1038/s41467-021-24764-8 (independent confirmation of the Stark effect)

sources: Sie et al., Nature Materials 14, 290 (2015), doi:10.1038/nmat4156
gaps: No momentum-space access; the connection to Floquet bands is model-based.
